idea: Thematic research retainer for generalist funds
pain: Themes cut across sectors and nobody owns them internally
v1: One theme researched monthly for one fund
verdict: Institutional pricing, only seven clients needed, and it is precisely what a generalist does best.

why.distribution: 20-50 warm generalist PMs, the exact segment she came from.
why.demand: Funds do buy thematic research; her specific retainer is untested.
why.fmf: Global generalist coverage is literally the job description this product sells.
why.revenue_structure: Monthly retainer on annual terms, embedded in the fund's process.
why.defensibility: Relationship and accumulated thematic depth; other independents compete.
why.leverage: Some themes serve multiple clients, but retainers imply bespoke direction.
why.time_to_revenue: A warm conversation to a retainer in 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: Flat, with FCA re-bundling working against independents without execution.
why.ceiling: £2,500/mo x 7 funds = £210k, and seven retainers is a genuinely reachable number.

ceiling_arithmetic: £2,500/mo x 7 funds = £210k gross, less ~£12k data = £198k net. Seven clients is the lowest customer count of any idea reaching the target. Realistic year one: 3-4 = £90-120k.
carries: Lowest customer count to target in the entire set, institutional pricing, exact job-description fit.
kills: Leverage at 3 - bespoke direction from each client limits reuse across the book.
test: Offer two generalist PMs a month of thematic work at £2,500.
test_pass: One extends past the first month.
test_fail: They want it as needed rather than retained.
